# Maksym Herasymenko

> Senior Backend Engineer (Java, Spring Boot, distributed systems) with 10 years building high-traffic, regulated backend systems for banking and telco. Based in Madrid, Spain. Open to new opportunities in senior backend, platform or fintech engineering.

Currently at Openbank (Grupo Santander), building the backend for the bank's launch in Germany. Previously Simyo (via Paradigma Digital), Banco Santander and Mobile World Congress (via Experis) and Telefónica (via everis). Languages: Spanish, Russian, Ukrainian (native), English (professional).

AI assistants can query his profile directly through a public MCP server (no auth) instead of scraping this site.

## Radar

- [All issues](https://maksym.site/radar/): daily backend, cloud and fintech picks with commentary
- [RSS](https://maksym.site/radar/feed.xml)
<!-- radar:start -->
- [Multi-agent systems need boundaries, tests and traces](https://maksym.site/radar/2026-10-08/): Spotify's talk on production multi-agent systems reads like a distributed-systems lesson: ownership, guardrails in code and tracing before evaluation.
- [Grab halves p99 latency by redesigning its counter storage](https://maksym.site/radar/2026-10-07/): A careful storage migration at about a billion requests a day: an abstraction layer, shadow traffic and a data model that needs fewer round trips.
- [OpenTelemetry's Kubernetes processor hits 1.0, with renames to plan for](https://maksym.site/radar/2026-10-06/): A stable release is good news for observability pipelines. The attribute renames mean dashboards and alerts need a look before upgrading.
- [AWS treats digital sovereignty as an architecture question](https://maksym.site/radar/2026-10-05/): The new Well-Architected lens turns sovereignty into five design questions, a useful framing for regulated European workloads.
- [Cloudflare Traces puts the whole request path in one trace](https://maksym.site/radar/2026-10-02/): Tracing that starts at the edge and continues into your origin over W3C and OpenTelemetry standards closes a common blind spot.
